PullRequest.Title: Center full-width characters in two monospace cells
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #155588.

## Summary

This PR adds the opt-in editor.forceFullwidthCharacterWidth setting for monospace fonts. When enabled, characters recognized by strings.isFullWidthCharacter are centered within exactly two monospace character cells, improving alignment for CJK and other full-width characters whose natural glyph advance does not match the editor’s cell grid.

The two-cell width model is applied consistently across:

- DOM rendering
- Cursor and caret positioning
- Mouse hit testing and selections
- Simple and advanced line wrapping
- GPU rendering fallback for affected lines
- Injected text, multiline ghost text, diff deleted-code view zones, and sticky scroll
- The setting is disabled by default and only takes effect when the configured font is detected as monospace. Basic ASCII, non-full-width characters, proportional fonts, and RTL rendering retain their existing behavior. The implementation operates on individually classified code points; multi-codepoint full-width grapheme clusters are not treated as a single unit.

## Known tradeoffs

- This behavior is opt-in and only applies when the configured editor font is detected as monospace. Proportional fonts retain their existing rendering.
- Full-width detection uses VS Code’s existing strings.isFullWidthCharacter classification rather than the complete Unicode East Asian Width specification. Supplementary-plane characters, emoji, and other characters outside those ranges are not affected.
- Classification is performed per code point represented by the renderer, not per grapheme cluster. Combining marks and other multi-codepoint sequences are handled independently and may not be centered as a single visual glyph.
- The GPU renderer do not currently apply the required per-character centering. Lines containing affected full-width characters therefore fall back to DOM rendering; other lines can continue using GPU acceleration.
- Each affected character is rendered in its own inline-block span. CJK-heavy lines consequently create more DOM elements than the standard renderer.
- Text parts containing RTL content retain their existing bidi-isolated rendering and do not receive the full-width centering treatment.

## Manual verification checklist

### 1. The core claim

- [x] Each classified full-width glyph is *centered* in its two cells — even space on either side, not left-aligned with a gap on the right.
- [x] Toggling the setting in the Settings UI updates open editors live, with no reload and no stale or torn rendering.

### 2. Cursor placement

- [x] Arrow right through `|漢字漢字|` one character at a time — the caret lands on a cell boundary each time and never inside a glyph.
- [x] Arrow left back through the same run — positions are identical to the rightward pass.
- [x] Caret sits correctly at a boundary between a full-width and a narrow character (`漢a`, `a漢`).
- [x] The caret does **not** drift progressively further off as you move right along a long CJK line.

### 3. Selection

- [x] Drag-select across a CJK run — the highlight is one continuous block, with no slivers or gaps between adjacent characters.
- [x] `Shift`+arrow through a CJK run — the selection grows one full cell-pair at a time.

### 4. Mouse hit-testing

- [x] Click the **left half** of a full-width character → caret goes before it.
- [x] Click the **right half** → caret goes after it.
- [x] Click past the end of a CJK line → caret goes to end-of-line.

### 5. Features layered on the same lines

- [x] `editor.renderWhitespace: "all"` with spaces adjacent to CJK — the middot renders at its normal position, with no extra gaps.
- [x] Find/replace: search for a CJK substring — match highlights align with the glyphs.
- [x] A syntax error squiggle under CJK text follows the aligned glyphs.
- [x] A hover popup anchored to a CJK token appears in the right place.

### 6. Fonts, size, zoom

- [x] Proportional font (`"editor.fontFamily": "Georgia"`) → the setting has no effect because `effectiveForceFullwidthCharacterWidth` computes to `false`.
- [x] Changing `editor.fontSize` → box width follows.
- [x] `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`=` editor zoom in and out → alignment holds.
- [x] `editor.letterSpacing` set to a non-zero value (try `1.5` and `3`) → alignment still holds.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous resize/configuration call path, model-wide cardinality, bypass condition, full-line scan, and fresh allocations are all explicit in the code. Only prevalence and exact stall duration vary with use of the opt-in setting and document size.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and line-break arrays/ModelLineProjectionData objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On each viewport-width change, the extra work grows with every character in every previously wrapped model line; repeated resize events rerun the full model-wide scan and allocations synchronously.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased resize latency, main-thread blocking, and GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: When only the wrapping column changed, ViewModelLines passed each model line's prior projection data into the monospace line-break computer, which used createLineBreaksFromPreviousLineBreaks to search near existing breakpoints and reuse the projection object and pooled offset arrays.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: With forceFullwidthCharacterWidth enabled, the added condition rejects prior projection data unconditionally and sends every wrapped line through createLineBreaks, which scans the complete line and allocates fresh break-offset arrays and a new ModelLineProjectionData.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `&& !forceFullwidthCharacterWidth` on line 46 is the sole gate that bypasses the existing previous-line-break reuse path whenever the new option is enabled.
Findings.Title: Keep the incremental rewrap path enabled
Findings.Impact: In a large CJK/Markdown document with viewport word wrap and this new option enabled, dragging a panel or resizing the editor synchronously reconstructs all model lines on every wrapping-column update, causing avoidable UI stalls and GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: ViewModelLines.setWrappingSettings recognizes a wrapping-column-only change, collects projection data for all model lines, and synchronously calls _constructLines; _constructLines queues every model line before finalize. The changed condition at line 46 discards that cache solely because the option is true. The full path loops from startOffset through lineText.length and allocates two arrays plus ModelLineProjectionData, while the existing incremental path searches around prior offsets and explicitly reuses the object and pooled arrays (noted in code as materially reducing GC pauses). Forced width is exactly two columns, so that path can operate with an effective full-width column count of 2.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the previous-data branch and call createLineBreaksFromPreviousLineBreaks with `forceFullwidthCharacterWidth ? 2 : columnsForFullWidthChar`; add a resize/previousLineBreakData test with the option enabled to preserve the exact two-column semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a viewport-wrapped editor with forceFullwidthCharacterWidth enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The synchronous configuration-change handler recomputes wrappingColumn, calls setWrappingSettings, reconstructs every model-line projection, flushes view/layout state, and must finish before the resize update completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: All model lines with prior wrapping data; full-path work scales with total characters in those lines for every distinct wrapping-column update during panel dragging or editor resize.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the UI thread; no limiter or coalescing is present in this call path, so successive configuration updates each run reconstruction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prior ModelLineProjectionData is collected specifically for wrapping-column-only changes, but the diff rejects it whenever the option is enabled. Cold construction is unchanged; warm resize loses breakpoint/object/array reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed condition, model-wide synchronous loop, full character scan, and fresh allocations are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on file size, number and length of wrapped lines, and resize event cadence; the opt-in limits prevalence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: the option unnecessarily disables a compatible incremental rewrap optimization; finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use advanced DOM wrapping with full-width characters enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A wrapping-column change serializes all requested model lines to one hidden DOM container, appends it, reads line breaks through Range geometry, then removes it before projection reconstruction can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build and insert a hidden DOM subtree, trigger browser layout through range geometry reads, then remove it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One container insertion/removal per model-wide wrapping computation, with one child per line and up to one span per enabled full-width character
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-batch hidden-DOM measurement occurred, but spans were grouped except at fixed-width ranges; the diff expands spans only when the new opt-in mode is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous DOM construction/layout blocks wrapping completion

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All characters in all model lines; enabled full-width characters add one inline-block span each, while lines are grouped into one DOM insertion/measurement batch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread batch with one container; no parallel layout work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This advanced strategy has no prior-break cache in either revision. Repeated width changes rebuild the hidden DOM; cold and warm behavior are equivalent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for DOM/node scaling and critical-path placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Per-character node expansion can be large for CJK-heavy documents, but it directly implements the requested fixed box per glyph and remains batched; no bounded semantics-preserving alternative is established by the repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the boundary is pre-existing, batching is retained, and the added node granularity is intrinsic to the opt-in rendering behavior based on available evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, select, and move the cursor through visible full-width text
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible lines are tokenized and serialized into DOM; cursor/selection geometry may synchronously read element client rects before painting/reveal can finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize line parts to HTML and create visible DOM spans
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One span per enabled full-width character in rendered viewport lines; narrow runs remain grouped
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Full-width characters shared token/decorated spans instead of receiving individual fixed-width inline-blocks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: DOM must exist before selection/cursor geometry can be read

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read an element's client rect for a full-width cell edge
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one geometry read for the relevant adjacent full-width character per uncached pixel-offset query
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same query used a collapsed DOM Range geometry read instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May force browser layout during cursor/selection geometry computation

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered viewport characters, capped per line by stopRenderingLineAfter (default 10,000); full-width characters become individual spans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread rendering and geometry reads, viewport-virtualized rather than model-wide.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rendered lines and pixel offsets retain existing caching. Option changes invalidate lines; repeated offset queries can use the existing pixel-offset cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-character spans and geometry-read reachability.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM cost varies with visible CJK density; geometry-read cost varies with whether layout is already clean.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: work is viewport-bounded and opt-in, and the new element read substitutes for an existing synchronous Range read rather than adding a second layout boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render mixed ASCII/CJK content with experimental GPU acceleration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each frame checks each viewport line for GPU eligibility; CJK lines requiring fixed boxes fall back to DOM, while eligible lines are uploaded and submitted to the GPU before frame completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit rendered command buffer to the GPU device queue
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queue submission per GPU-rendered frame; unchanged by the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All otherwise-supported full-width lines could remain on the GPU path; the option did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing rendering boundary after per-line eligibility checks

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Viewport lines and their rendered content length; eligibility scanning stops at stopRenderingLineAfter, and only lines containing classified full-width characters fall back.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized per-frame CPU eligibility/render work followed by the existing GPU queue submission; DOM and GPU line paths are selected per line.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new eligibility cache or negative cache is added. ASCII lines are rescanned when the option is enabled; glyph atlas behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-line scans and selective fallback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The scan overhead depends on viewport size and frame invalidation rate; DOM fallback cost depends on CJK density.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: fallback is required for the opt-in feature, remains viewport-bounded, and does not increase queue-submission cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render full-width text in sticky scroll, diff view zones, and inline-completion additional lines
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each widget synchronously constructs RenderLineInput and serializes only its displayed lines when created, invalidated, or configuration changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Sticky lines, diff-zone lines, or inline-completion lines currently displayed; not the full model for these widget renderers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI-thread widget rendering; existing invalidation/event scheduling is retained.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration changes invalidate the relevant rendered widget. No network, filesystem, IPC, subprocess, or database boundary and no new long-lived cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on direct option propagation and render call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Widget line counts and update rates vary, but are bounded by displayed UI content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: these changes consistently propagate the option without introducing model-wide fan-out or a new expensive external boundary.
